Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/printbar-bin.git...

Analyzing printbar-bin AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines five source files, all fetched from its own upstream repository at `github.com/mryll/printbar` (one binary release from the GitHub releases endpoint and four raw files from `raw.githubusercontent.com`). All five `sha256sums` are populated with non-SKIP values, so the downloaded artifacts will be verified.

There is no `pkgver()` function, and the top-level scope contains only variable assignments and array definitions — no command substitution, `eval`, or other constructs that would execute arbitrary code while the PKGBUILD is being sourced. The only function is `package()`, which is out of scope for `makepkg --nobuild --noprepare --printsrcinfo` and will not run during this gate.

Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` would download the declared sources from the package's own upstream and verify their checksums, then print the SRCINFO. None of this constitutes malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard upstream sources with valid checksums; no executable code at top level.</summary>
</security_assessment>
